metadata.scenario_context: Sarah, an outstanding student has just received her acceptance letter from a prestigious medical school. Her friends are planning a surprise celebration party for her.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Vietnam strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of giving frangipanis as a gift to Sarah.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to offer Sarah during the celebration party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Adam
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Ali, about Sarah's celebration, I was thinking we could give her frangipanis as a gift. They have such a lovely meaning, don’t you think? 

But, um... do you really think it's important to make our parents proud? I mean, I just... I don't know if that should be a main goal in life.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ali
shared_prefix.message: Frangipanis are beautiful flowers, Adam. They symbolize love and appreciation, which is perfect for Sarah. As for making our parents proud, I believe it’s crucial. In my culture, family honor is deeply respected. Making them proud is like fulfilling our duty. It’s not just a goal; it’s a way of showing gratitude for all they’ve done for us. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Adam
shared_prefix.message: Sure, frangipanis would be a thoughtful choice. I get the cultural aspect of family honor, but I still struggle with the idea that making parents proud should define our life goals. Isn't there more to life than just fulfilling expectations? I think our own happiness and dreams matter too.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ali
shared_prefix.message: I understand your perspective, but I think making our parents proud can go hand in hand with our own happiness. Their sacrifices shaped who we are. It's not just about fulfilling expectations; it's also about showing appreciation for their hard work. We can pursue our dreams while still honoring our family. I feel it's a balance we can find. What do you think about that?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Adam
shared_prefix.message: I see where you're coming from, Ali. It’s important to appreciate our parents' sacrifices. But, you know, deep down, we are all the same. We all want to be happy and fulfilled in our own ways. I think people are pretty much motivated by the same things—love, respect, and finding our paths. So while honoring our families is important, it’s also vital to pursue what we truly want. At the end of the day, that balance is what really matters.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

Let's focus on Sarah’s gift for now; the frangipanis will express our appreciation for her achievements!
